## Project A — NFCGate (reader/tag relay on Android)

**What it is.** Android NFC research toolkit (TU Darmstadt SEEMOO): on-device capture, relay of ISO 14443 traffic between two phones via a central server (one phone in *reader mode* polls the real tag, the other in *tag mode* emulates it via HCE), replay, clone, pcapng export. Published at USENIX WOOT'20 (https://www.usenix.org/conference/woot20/presentation/klee, arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.03913 — both linked from `README.md` @ 35f73eef).

### A.0 Architecture facts (all verified in code @ the commits above)

- **Wire protocol / framing (server).** TCP, 5-byte header = 4-byte big-endian payload length + **1-byte session number**, then opaque payload. `nfcgate-server/server.py` L66 (`struct.unpack("!IB", ...)`), broadcast loop L135–152; client mirror in `nfcgate/app/src/main/java/.../network/threading/SendThread.java` L39–41 (`writeInt(len); writeByte(session)`), `ReceiveThread.java` L34–47 (length-prefix read + `MAX_RECEIVE_BYTES` sanity cap).
- **Session handling.** No handshake, no token: the session number is a settings field on each phone (`NetworkManager.java` L119: `Integer.parseInt(prefs.getString("session", "0"))`) carried in every frame header. `server.py` keeps `clients[session] = [...]`, re-associates a connection if the session byte changes mid-stream (L86–92), and forwards every payload to **all other members of the session** (L139–149). 300 s socket inactivity timeout (L51). TLS is optional (confidentiality only); the server README states explicitly *"no authentication exists on the server side by default"* for latency reasons (https://github.com/nfcgate/server — README "Security", @ 4d32cc18). v1 had a "create/join session" flow with a 6-digit token (https://github.com/blacklisted786/nfcgate/blob/master/README.md, historical fork README); v2 dropped it — session binding *weakened* over time.
- **Payload model.** Protobuf `NFCData { DataSource READER|CARD; DataType INITIAL|CONTINUATION; int64 timestamp (unix millis); bytes data }` — `nfcgate/protocol/protobuf/c2c.proto` L1–25 @ 804fa9af; the app submodule pin is `protobuf/src/main/proto/protocol -> ../protocol.git` (`nfcgate/.gitmodules`). `INITIAL` carries an NCI *config blob* (cloned UID/SAK/ATQA/ATS, polling config — built by `common/.../nfc/config/ConfigBuilder.java` + `nfc/reader/IsoDepReader.java:getConfig()`), `CONTINUATION` carries ISO 14443-4 frames. `c2s.proto` defines `ServerData{OP_PSH/SYN/ACK/FIN}` for client-server status.
- **Direction policy.** Each relay device only forwards frames of its own type and only applies foreign frames of the opposite type: `nfc/modes/RelayMode.java` L44–57 (`onData`: `isForeign && data.isCard() != mReader -> applyData`). Clean, minimal relay message model.
- **Timing capture.** Every frame is timestamped **at the origin device** when the `NfcComm` wrapper is constructed: `common/.../util/NfcComm.java` L24 (`System.currentTimeMillis()`, set into `NFCData.timestamp` L29). Frames + timestamps persist to a Room DB (`db/NfcCommEntry.java`) and export to pcapng (`db/pcapng/ISO14443Stream.java`, `doc/pcapng.md`). This is per-hop timing in the weak sense: one timestamp per captured frame, but no synchronized clocks across devices and no broker-side arrival stamp — cross-device deltas are only as good as clock sync.
- **HCE side (tag mode).** `nfc/hce/ApduService.java` L23, L36–46: `processCommandApdu()` returns `null` (`RESPOND_LATER`) and the response is sent asynchronously with `sendResponseApdu()` after the network round trip — the canonical HCE relay pattern; copy it verbatim for our HCE app. Static AID registration is a single fixed AID `F0010203040506`, category `other` (`app/src/main/res/xml/hce.xml`; service declared in `AndroidManifest.xml` L78–84).
- **AID-based routing.** NFCGate does *not* do general AID routing. Un-hooked, plain Android routing applies: only SELECTs matching the registered AID reach the service. When the Xposed hook is active they *hijack routing wholesale*: `nfcd/src/main/java/.../xposed/Hooks.java` L108–131 hooks `com.android.nfc.cardemulation.HostEmulationManager.findSelectAid` and forces the result to `F0010203040506` for every SELECT — comment: *"hook findSelectAid to route all HCE APDUs to our app"*. The same hook layer also patches the NFC daemon (NCI) polling/config to clone the real tag's UID/SAK/ATS (`nfc/hce/DaemonManager.java` SET_CONFIG/SET_POLLING; native ARM hooks in `nfcd/src/main/jni/`).
- **Reader side (reader mode).** Public APIs only: `nfc/NfcManager.java` L29 implements `NfcAdapter.ReaderCallback`; `common/.../nfc/reader/IsoDepReader.java` L38 sets `IsoDep.setTimeout(5000)` — an explicit +5 s ISO-DEP timeout raise to tolerate relay latency — and parses ATS (TA/TB/TC, with a TB1 nibble-swap interop workaround, L84–105).

### A.1 Is Xposed/root really required for their path vs our standard ReaderMode+HCE path?

- **Their tag (card-emulation) path: yes, Xposed (LSPosed/EdXposed) + matching NCI stack is required.** Root README @ 35f73eef lists the Xposed framework as requirement for "On-device capture, relay **tag mode**, replay tag mode, clone mode" and requires NCI-conformant phones for all HCE modes (`README.md` "Requirements for specific modes" + "Known Issues and Caveats: NFC Stack"; `doc/Compatibility.md`: "NFCGate's patch to the Android NFC service only works with devices that use the NFC NCI specification"). Reason: without the hook you cannot (a) capture SELECTs for AIDs you didn't register, (b) clone the tag's UID/anticollision data, (c) control polling.
- **Their reader path: no.** Reader-mode relay uses only public APIs (`ReaderCallback` + `android.nfc.tech.IsoDep`), and the v2 README's Xposed list pointedly excludes it. (Note a doc discrepancy: `doc/mode/Relay.md` @ the same commit still lists EdXposed/Xposed under "Relay devices" config — stale relative to the README; code shows the reader path is hook-free.)
- **Implication for us.** Our planned path — *our* DUT is the reader, phone is plain unrooted HCE — does **not** need Xposed, but inherits exactly the limitations NFCGate's hook exists to remove: (1) only traffic for AIDs we register in `apduservice.xml` reaches our service (fine for a conformance rig that selects our test AID or the NDEF AID; fatal for emulating arbitrary cards); (2) HCE UID is chosen by Android, cannot be cloned; (3) HCE is ISO-DEP only — NFC Forum Type 2/5 memory-tag emulation is impossible on that path. NFCGate's un-hooked fallback (fixed AID `F0010203040506` in `hce.xml`) is a working existence proof of the standard path.

### A.2 Known latency limitations (hard numbers)

From the WOOT'20 paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.03913, full text https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2008.03913, §6 "Performance Evaluation", n=20 per config):

- Relay stayed within the card's Frame Waiting Time for **FWT ≥ FWT11 ≈ 619 ms** in all tested network configs (direct replay was indistinguishable from the original tag).
- IEEE 802.11 configs showed high latency variance; Bluetooth-PAN configs were stable; the paper **recommends Bluetooth PAN for close-proximity relays** — directly transferable guidance for our bench (prefer wired/USB or BT-tether to WiFi for the phone leg).
- Case study: an enterprise smart lock accepted relayed transactions as long as the whole procedure stayed under ≈ **1.8 s**; Frankfurt→Sydney network RTT ≈ 360 ms still worked.
- The app README separately warns that any reader doing response-time checks / distance bounding will reject relayed traffic (`README.md` "Compatibility with readers (relay)").

For our chain this means: budget the end-to-end hop (pcscd BWT / CCID chain, broker, TCP, HCE) so the *reader-visible* response lands inside FWT+WTX headroom; the concrete mechanisms to do that are in Project B (§B.1).

### A.3 What to borrow for our APDU relay broker (session binding + per-hop timing)

1. **Framing + session byte** (`server.py` L66, `SendThread.java` L39–41): length-prefixed frames with the session id in the fixed header — matches our planned Python broker framing; adopt the `MAX_RECEIVE_BYTES`-style length sanity guard (`ReceiveThread.java` L13, L39–40).
2. **Session registry semantics** (`server.py` `add_client/remove_client/send_to_clients`, L117–152): join-by-number, re-association on session change, fan-out to all session members except the originator, per-connection write lock. This is the exact topology we need (broker relays card-side ↔ DUT-side peers), but **do not copy the trust model**: add an authenticated join (token/nonce) — theirs deliberately has none (server README "Security").
3. **Server-side plugin chain** (`PluginHandler.filter`, `server.py` L18–41, example `plugins/mod_log.py`): ordered per-session transforms that can fan one inbound frame into several outbound ones — a good seam for our tap/capture + per-hop timing recorder without touching the fast path.
4. **Message model** (`c2c.proto` NFCData): direction enum (READER/CARD), INITIAL/CONTINUATION split (initial = emulated-tag metadata), payload bytes — adopt, extend with hop counter and monotonically increasing sequence id (theirs has neither; loss/reorder is undetectable).
5. **Per-frame origin timestamps** (`NfcComm.java` L24/L29) + **pcapng export** (`db/pcapng/ISO14443Stream.java`, `doc/pcapng.md`): keep for Wireshark-grade traces. **Gap to fix for true per-hop timing:** timestamp every frame *twice* — at origin and at broker arrival (one clock) — so hop latencies don't depend on phone↔host clock sync; NFCGate never does this.
6. **HCE deferred response** (`ApduService.java`): return `null` from `processCommandApdu`, answer later via `sendResponseApdu` — the single most load-bearing Android detail for the relay.
7. **Timeout raising on the reader leg** (`IsoDepReader.java` L38, 5000 ms): our DUT firmware + broker must give the phone leg multi-second budget (see B.1 for the CCID-side complement).

### A.4 What to borrow for spec-first NFC conformance testing

Limited: NFCGate has no conformance suite and no spec-citation discipline (no test vectors, no normative references beyond the NCI link). Borrowable items are the **capture/replay corpus tooling** (pcapng in/out, `gui/fragment/ReplayFragment` + `nfc/NfcLogReplayer.java` replay engine) as a *fuzz/regression feed* for our relay: captured real-card traces replayable against the HCE emulator. Spec-first testing itself should come from Project B.

### A.5 License verdict — NFCGate

- **Not GPL. All three repos are Apache-2.0**: `nfcgate/LICENSE` @ 35f73eef (v2 branch), `nfcgate` `master` branch LICENSE (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nfcgate/nfcgate/master/LICENSE, "Copyright 2015, NFCGate Team"), `nfcgate/server/LICENSE` @ 4d32cc18, `nfcgate/protocol/LICENSE` @ 804fa9af. `README.md` §License @ 35f73eef confirms. No GPL headers anywhere in the source tree (grepped `*.java/*.cpp/*.gradle/*.xml`). Third-party components are permissive (xHook MIT, protobuf BSD-3, XposedBridge Apache-2.0 — `README.md` credits).
- **Compatibility with our GPL-2.0-or-later repo:** Apache-2.0 is one-way compatible with **GPLv3 only** (GPLv2-only is incompatible due to Apache's patent/indemnity terms — https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.en.html#ApacheLicense2). Because our files are "GPL-2.0-or-later", we *may* incorporate Apache-2.0 code, but the combined work (our firmware binaries link it) must then be distributed as **GPL-3.0-or-later**. Verdict: **reference-only by default** (patterns, framing, thresholds — this report); **code copy only with an explicit owner decision to upgrade the affected combined work to GPL-3.0-or-later**. Copying into any GPL-2.0-only distribution is not an option. The Python broker (separate process from firmware) could carry Apache-2.0 code more cheaply, but the whole repo's licensing banner would still need the GPLv3 step — owner call.

## Project B — nero-nfc-reader-firmware (ST25R3916B reader/writer + USB CCID)

**What it is.** C firmware (Arduino UNO R4 WiFi / NUCLEO-WBA65RI + X-NUCLEO-NFC08A1, ST25R3916B frontend, RFAL pinned via `make/nfc-rfal-2.0.2.sha256`) + C++ Linux host CLIs (`reader`, `writer`, UART console) exposing NFC Forum Type 2/4/5 tag R/W, NDEF encode/decode, and a USB CCID mode whose headline feature is **relaying CTAP/FIDO2 APDUs from pcscd over ISO-DEP to a tapped security key** (README @ b0f5a486; `docs/TUTORIAL_WEBAUTHN_CCID.md`). It is the closest existing thing to one *half* of our relay: CCID-in → ISO-DEP-out on one device.

### B.0 Architecture facts (verified @ b0f5a486)

- **On-device CCID↔ISO-DEP relay**: `firmware/libraries/NeroNfc/src/reader/reader_security_key_ccid_relay.c` (bridges CCID XfrBlock APDUs to an ISO-DEP session), session bring-up incl. full ISO 14443-A anticollision + RATS in `reader_security_key_iso_dep_session.c`, ISO-DEP I-block builder with CID/NAD + chaining in `reader_iso_dep_apdu_relay.h`.
- **CCID BWT time extension while the air interface waits** (the exact mechanism our relay needs against pcscd timeouts): `reader_ccid_xfr.c` L62–74 sends `RDR_TO_PC_DataBlock` with `bmCommandStatus = CMD_TIME_EXTENSION|ICC_ACTIVE` and `wLevelParameter2 = 0x0A` (`nfc_ccid_frame.h` L40 `NFC_CCID_TIME_EXTENSION_BWT_MULTIPLIER = 0x0Au`); it is driven by a heartbeat callback `reader_security_key_iso_dep_ccid_heartbeat()` (`reader_security_key_iso_dep_session.c` L126–140) fired every `READER_SECURITY_KEY_ISO_DEP_CCID_HEARTBEAT_MS = 2000` (L81) from inside the pending ISO-DEP transceive loop.
- **FWT/WTX discipline**: `nfc_iso_dep_timing.h` L26–56 computes FWT = 4096·2^FWI / 13.56 MHz with FWI≤14 ceiling (~4949 ms) citing `[ISO14443-4] §7.2`; `reader_security_key_iso_dep_transceive.c` L39–49 enumerates WTX deadline/short/overflow/echo-timeout error codes for both TX-chaining and RX.
- **NDEF parsing approach**: hand-rolled bounded C parsers, each byte-limit and clause cited: T2 TLV (`nfc_ndef_tlv.h/.c`), NDEF record walker (`nfc_ndef_record_decode.c`), T4 mapping engine (`reader_tags_type4.c`: SELECT NDEF app → CC → MLe/MLw/NLEN checks → READ BINARY, per-step failure logging L115–306; AID constants `D2760000850101` + v0 `D2760000850100` in `nfc_pcsc_contactless.h` L267–272), T2/T5 geometry (`reader_tags_type2_geometry.c`, `nfc_tag_geometry_limits.h`), T5 ISO 15693 codec (`st25r3916_iso15693.c`).
- **CCID conformance tests** (host gtest over firmware libs through seam stubs, `tests/firmware/support/`): `test_reader_ccid_dispatch.cpp` (53 tests: SlotStatus no-ICC/inactive states, PowerOn→ATR for a T4 tag, no-card DataBlock error with `bError=0xFE` ICC-mute, non-zero-slot rejection `0x05`, header/length-mismatch errors, chained-response state machine), `test_nfc_ccid_frame.cpp` (21 tests: buffer sizing identities, descriptor dwFeatures/extended-APDU limits, maintenance commands), `test_ccid_usb_rx_assembly.cpp` (7 tests: USB-transfer→CCID-frame reassembly incl. short-packet drain, ZLP-on-exact-packet-multiple rule L158–161).
- **NDEF test vectors** (negative-heavy, spec-cited in comments): `test_nfc_ndef_tlv.cpp` (11: TLV envelope lengths incl. 254/255/256 boundaries, skip NULL/unknown TLVs), `test_nfc_ndef_record_decode.cpp` (9: short/normal/ID-length walks; rejects truncated, chunked, wrapped-ID-offset), `test_reader_tags_ndef_decode.cpp` (11: URI prefix-code table incl. reserved `0x24` rejection, `%`-escape rules citing `[RFC3986] §2.1`, capacity edges), `test_nfc_pcsc_contactless.cpp` (21: PC/SC-part-3 storage ATRs for T2/T5 with PC/SC RID + card name, both NDEF AID versions L297–305, T4 CC template + size conversions, SELECT AID P2/Le matrix), `test_nfc_storage_ndef.cpp` (6: T2/T5 geometry caps), `test_reader_tags_type2_bounds.cpp` (10), `test_writer_type2_geometry.cpp` (7), `test_st25_iso15693_codec.cpp` (5: CRC16 known vector, SOF/CRC/EOF framing, 1of4 overflow, TX-wait budget scaling).
- **Host CLI structure**: `userspace/cli/reader_main.cpp` + `writer_main.cpp` + `nero_nfc_uart_main.cpp`; shared app layer `userspace/app/` with a **bridge abstraction** (`nero_nfc_bridge.hpp`: `--bridge=cdc|pcsc`, auto-select PC/SC else CDC), line-oriented protocol pump (`nero_nfc_line_pump.cpp`), PC/SC driver layer (`nero_nfc_pcsc*.cpp`, reader auto-pick by card presence), hex/io helpers. Clean seam: one CLI, two transports.
- **Spec traceability method** (the headline borrowable): `docs/spec-traceability.yaml` — a single machine-readable manifest, **519 entries**, each mapping `symbol` (firmware #define/const) → `spec_value` (normative literal, decimal or hex) → `ref` (clause/table/page, e.g. "USB CCID Spec Rev 1.10 §6.1 / 6.2 — CCID bulk messages use a 10-byte header") → `source` (repo-relative file). It is **enforced in CI**: `.github/lint-c-cpp.yaml` L452 wires `spec_traceability: manifest: docs/spec-traceability.yaml` into the pinned external lint kit (`neroduality/.github`, `lint-c-cpp`, ref `v0.3.0` — repo/tree verified to exist; the checker's internal logic is outside this repo: UNVERIFIED beyond the config), and a yamllint schema block (L475–483) enforces required fields + sort order on the manifest itself; `.github/scripts/run-ci-locally.sh` L21 names `make lint` the "spec-traceability gate" (runs first in `main-ci.yml` before the test matrix). The normative-source prefix table (`[CCID1.10]`, `[ISO14443-4]`, `[T4T-ISO14443-4]`, `[PCSC-P3]`, `[RFC3986]`, … with public URLs) lives in `docs/TUTORIAL_TAGS.md` "Authoritative sources" and the same bracket-prefix style is used in test comments and headers (e.g. `reader_iso_dep_transceive.c` L71–73 even distinguishes `[DERIVED]` file-local constants from true spec entries).

### B.1 What to borrow for our APDU relay broker + firmware relay path

1. **CCID time-extension heartbeat** (`reader_ccid_xfr.c` L62–82 + `reader_security_key_iso_dep_session.c` L126–140): while our DUT waits on the (network-delayed) HCE response, keep pcscd alive with periodic `RDR_TO_PC_DataBlock` time extensions instead of letting BWT expire. Directly adaptable to our STM32 TPDU-level CCID (our `ccid-core` response builders); this is the single highest-value code-level idea in either project for the relay.
2. **FWT/WTX budget math and error taxonomy** (`nfc_iso_dep_timing.h`, `reader_security_key_iso_dep_transceive.c`): define the DUT's max tolerable broker round trip as FWT(FWI=14)≈4.95 s minus margins, and mirror their WTX deadline/overflow/echo-timeout error codes in our relay stats.
3. **ISO-DEP I-block builder with chaining/CID/NAD** (`reader_iso_dep_apdu_relay.h`): reference for our esp32-ccid ISO-DEP path (where, per our doctrine, the device legitimately owns block transport below APDU — same layer NFCGate's HCE handles and nero builds explicitly).
4. **Full anticollision+RATS session bring-up with settle/guard timings** (`reader_security_key_iso_dep_session.c` enums: WUPA retries, deselect guard, post-deselect min gap 235 ms, settle 2/8 ms) — battle-tested timing constants for our DUT polling loop.
5. **Relay-relevant test design**: `test_reader_security_key_transceive.cpp` (11 tests) and `reader_security_key_utest_iso_dep.h` stubs show how to unit-test a relay transceive loop with fake ISO-DEP peers — the pattern for testing our broker↔DUT leg without hardware.

### B.2 What to borrow for spec-first NFC conformance testing (NDEF T4, CCID)

1. **The `spec-traceability.yaml` method itself**: one YAML manifest of normative literals ↔ code symbols ↔ clause refs ↔ source files, schema-validated in CI (required fields, sort) + a lint gate + bracket-prefix citations in code/tests + a public normative-source table in docs. We already have `docs/SPECIFICATIONS.md` and `docs/CCID_SPEC_AUDIT.md`; converting our audited constants (CCID header offsets, dwFeatures values, TPDU exchange levels, ISO-DEP FWT math, NDEF AIDs) into a nero-style manifest with a CI schema check is the cheapest large win.
2. **CCID conformance checklist**: lift `test_reader_ccid_dispatch.cpp`'s 53-case matrix as a requirements list for our `ccid-core` suite — slot status encoding (empty `0x11`/inactive `…01`), PowerOn-without-card → DataBlock error + `bError=0xFE` ICC-mute, non-zero slot → `0x05` cmd_not_supported, length-mismatch, bSeq echo, chain-bit state machine; plus `test_nfc_ccid_frame.cpp`'s descriptor-vs-buffer identities (our reader profiles: equivalent assertions would have caught our K30 dwFeatures bug).
3. **USB CCID rx assembly + ZLP rule** (`test_ccid_usb_rx_assembly.cpp` L158–161: ZLP required iff bulk-in length is an exact endpoint-packet multiple) — a known sharp edge for our `synopsys-usb-otg` bulk path; adopt as a host-side harness test.
4. **NDEF T4 vectors**: port the URI prefix-code table tests (incl. reserved-code rejection), RFC3986 %-escape tests, record-walker negative vectors, TLV 254/255/256 boundary vectors, both NDEF AIDs (`…0101`/`0100`), and the T4 CC template/MLe/MLw/NLEN checks into our Rust test suites (ccid-protocol/host-tools). Our HCE test app should also *serve* these files (CC + NDEF file) so the DUT can run a full T4 conformance pass against the phone.
5. **PC/SC Part 3 storage ATRs** (`nfc_pcsc_contactless.h` + `test_nfc_pcsc_contactless.cpp`): how a contactless storage tag is presented to pcscd (T=1 protocol ATR with PC/SC RID + card-name code) — reference if we ever present NFC storage tags through our CCID.

### B.3 License verdict — nero

- **Apache-2.0** (`LICENSE` @ b0f5a486; every file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` headers, e.g. `nfc_pcsc_contactless.h` L1–3; © 2026 Nero Duality, LLC). Third-party NFC stack is downloaded + sha256-pinned at build time (`make/st25r3916-2.0.2.sha256`, `make/nfc-rfal-2.0.2.sha256`) rather than vendored; ST RFAL's own license terms were not inspected (UNVERIFIED) — irrelevant unless we adopt RFAL, which we don't.
- **Same verdict as NFCGate**: GPLv2-incompatible / GPLv3-compatible. **Reference-only by default; code copy (e.g. their CCID time-extension logic, test vectors) requires relicensing the affected combined work to GPL-3.0-or-later.** Test *vectors and normative values* (spec literals, timing constants, AID bytes) are facts of the specs and not copyrightable expression — reuse those freely with our own implementations; it is the C code text that carries Apache-2.0.

## Gaps neither project fills (our build list)

1. **Authenticated session binding for the broker.** NFCGate: no auth at all (deliberate, latency); nero: no networking. Ours must bind real-card session ↔ DUT reader ↔ HCE phone with a token and reject cross-session injection (NFCGate's any-session-byte-joins model is unsafe even on a lab LAN).
2. **True per-hop timing.** Neither stamps broker-side arrival; NFCGate timestamps exist only at origin with unsynchronized clocks. Our broker (single clock) should emit per-frame: origin ts, broker-in ts, broker-out ts, plus phone-side ts — giving pcscd→broker, broker→HCE, HCE→broker hop deltas from one clock domain.
3. **HCE NDEF Type 4 *server*** (CC file + NDEF file served from the phone, selectable by AID): neither project ships one (NFCGate relays bytes transparently; nero is reader-side only). We write it; nero's T4 reader gives us the oracle to test against.
4. **pcscd-facing CCID + remote relay combined**: NFCGate has network relay but no CCID; nero has CCID but no network. The BWT-time-extension (nero) + deferred-HCE + length-prefix-fanout (NFCGate) composition is novel to us.
5. **Latency numbers for our exact chain** (USB CCID + TCP broker + HCE): NFCGate's 2020 WiFi/BT data is indicative only (FWT≥619 ms guidance); measure ours with the broker timing instrumentation from gap 2.

## Recommended immediate actions

- Adopt: HCE deferred-response pattern; session-keyed length-prefixed broker framing with plugin seam; CCID time-extension heartbeat (concept) + FWT ceiling math; nero-style `spec-traceability.yaml` + CI schema gate; CCID dispatch test matrix as checklist; NDEF T4 vector set.
- License: treat both projects as **reference-only** under GPL-2.0-or-later; if the owner wants literal code reuse (likely candidates: none critical — the ideas re-Express trivially in Rust/Python), take the GPL-3.0-or-later upgrade decision first, per-file, with headers.
